pronunciation.note: Izanagi is Tier 2: plain Hepburn. He is one of the two primordial creator kami of Japanese myth.

domains.title: He-Who-Invites
domains.subtitle: Creator of the Islands, Father of the Gods
domains.lead: Izanagi is the male half of the primordial creator pair. With his sister-wife Izanami, he stirred the primordial ocean with the spear Ame-no-Nuboko and raised the islands of Japan. His later journey to the underworld and ritual purification gave birth to the most powerful kami of the Japanese pantheon, including Amaterasu herself.

cards.name: Creator of Japan
cards.desc: With Izanami, he stirred the ocean and created the archipelago.

cards.name: Spear of Heaven
cards.desc: Ame-no-Nuboko, the jeweled spear with which he stirred the brine.

cards.name: Father of the Sun
cards.desc: His purification produced Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi, and Susanoo.

cards.name: Visitor to Yomi
cards.desc: He descended to the underworld to retrieve his dead wife Izanami.

mythology.lead: Izanagi's mythology is the creation narrative of the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki: the making of the world, the founding of death, and the birth of the gods who rule heaven and earth.

myths.title: The Creation of the Islands
myths.text: Standing on the Floating Bridge of Heaven, Izanagi and Izanami lowered the jeweled spear into the formless ocean. When they lifted it, brine dripped from the tip and congealed into the island of Onogoroshima. They descended to the island, circled the pillar of heaven, and began to create the Japanese archipelago.

myths.title: The Birth and Death of Izanami
myths.text: As Izanami gave birth to the fire god Kagutsuchi, she was burned so badly that she died. Izanagi pursued her to Yomi, the underworld, and asked her to return. She had already eaten the food of Yomi and could not leave, but she asked him to wait. When he broke his promise and lit a comb to see her decaying body, she sent the eight thunder demons and the hag of Yomi after him. He escaped and sealed the entrance with a great boulder.

myths.title: The Purification of Izanagi
myths.text: After escaping Yomi, Izanagi performed purification (misogi) in a river. As he washed, new kami were born from his discarded garments and from his body: Amaterasu from his left eye, Tsukuyomi from his right eye, and Susanoo from his nose. These three became the rulers of heaven, night, and sea.

lore.syncretism: Izanagi and Izanami are often compared to other creator couples across Eurasia, but their specifically Japanese features — the island-creating spear, the underworld separation, the birth of gods from purification — are distinct. In the modern period, Izanagi became a focus of State Shinto as a symbol of national origins, and the creation myth was taught in schools as literal history.
lore.culturalLegacy: Izanagi remains a foundational figure in Japanese myth. His name appears in shrine rituals, creation narratives, and popular retellings. The misogi purification ritual is still practiced at shrines and by practitioners of Shinto-derived martial arts. The image of the divine couple stirring the ocean is one of Japan's most enduring creation scenes.
lore.extendedMeditation: Izanagi is the one who could not bring back the dead. His grief produced the separation of life and death, and his purification produced the gods. His story suggests that creation and loss are inseparable: to make the world, something must be left behind.
lore.archaeology: Izanagi has no independent material cult separate from shrines honoring the creation kami as a pair. The Taga Taisha in Ōmi is one prominent shrine associated with Izanagi and Izanami. Creation imagery appears in shrine art and ritual objects across Japan.
